rationale:
Final design: the iteration-5 configuration, resubmitted unchanged. This is a score-preserving confirmation, not a new test. The race is deterministic per seed and track, so the expected score is 137.76 with oval progress near 0.55 and s-bend and slalom progress near 0.18 and 0.12.

Evidence: iteration 5 scored 137.7649 with base_speed 1.8 and kp 2.8. Iteration 6 and iteration 7 reproduced that score exactly. Iterations 2 and 4 (base 1.6, same otherwise) scored 132.0028, so the speed step gained about 5.8 points. That gain is net: the oval improved (progress 0.45 to 0.55, one extra finish at 1.925 s), while s-bend progress fell from 0.27 to 0.18 and slalom from 0.16 to 0.12. Mean s-bend and slalom scores fell from about 111 to 78 and from 67 to 52. Line loss on the bends fell to 0.0 at 1.8, so the bend failures are lateral off-track ends, not line losses.

What I accepted from the round-2 critique: (1) This iteration is a resubmission and cannot add parameter evidence, so I say so here. (2) The stale line-loss figures of 0.65 to 0.8 are from base 1.6. The measured value at 1.8 is 0.0 on the bends. (3) kp 2.8 is the raced value; kp 3.0 in the authorized text is a documentation error, and I keep 2.8 so the race matches the measured 137.76. (4) max_error is capped near 0.06 by the off-track rule, so it is not a decision input. (5) The bend progress loss is the main cost of the speed step and must be judged alongside the oval gain.

What I rejected: (a) base_speed 2.0. base_pwm reaches the 4095 ceiling there, so steering headroom on the outside wheel is lost exactly where the bends need it. (b) Any geometry, kp, ki or kd change in this race, since that would trade the best measured score for an untested design. (c) The claim that kp 2.8 and kd 1.0  'add no gain' is removed; those values were never raced. (d) A footprint or span change without a mechanism for the off-track end, since widening the span did not move max_error in iteration 1.

Success criterion for this iteration: the score must stay at or above 137.76, with s-bend and slalom progress not falling below their iteration-5 values.

Decision rule for the next round: if the score is confirmed at 137.76, the next single-variable test is ki 0.1, judged on total score and on s-bend and slalom progress, not on max_error. If bend progress remains the main loss, test a sensor footprint change only if it has a stated mechanism for lateral margin. Base_speed 2.0 is not tested because of wheel-command saturation.
